verdict.rationale: Maritime has its own trigger system, but the documented type is a cron schedule that wakes the agent and delivers a prompt. That is a time-based recurring schedule, not a general event-to-action rule. The only event-driven mechanism documented is outbound webhooks that POST on agent lifecycle events: a fixed notification action, not user-definable conditions and actions. missing for 10: documented event-based trigger types beyond cron, a user-defined rule/condition engine mapping arbitrary events to actions, examples of event-triggered actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: A cron trigger takes a standard five-field expression, wakes the agent on schedule, and delivers its `prompt` as a chat message on every fire.
Any Docker container becomes an agent: three endpoints get you sleep/wake, channels, and triggers.
Subscribe a URL, and Maritime POSTs a signed JSON body on every lifecycle event.
the platform syncs the schedule it sets for itself into real wake triggers
